commit.message:
Claude: RTC: Fix crash and heap overflow from a malformed RTCP packet. v8.0.73

A WebRTC peer could crash the server with one RTCP packet:

- A header length of 0 made the payload length negative, so read_bytes
  failed its assert and aborted the process (BYE, TWCC and every other
  type decoded by SrsRtcpCommon).
- A feedback packet (generic FB, NACK, PLI, SLI, RPSI) with length 1
  at the end of the compound read the media SSRC past the buffer and
  aborted the same way.
- A packet over 1500 bytes copied past the fixed payload_ buffer in
  SrsRtcpCommon and SrsRtcpTWCC, a heap overflow, because the UDP read
  buffer takes up to 64KB.

decode_header now rejects length 0, the feedback decoders reject
length < 2 before the media SSRC, and Common and TWCC reject a payload
larger than kRtcpPacketSize. SrsRtcpApp now starts with the length of
an empty APP packet, which it used to leave unset and which the new
check rejects.

Adds 9 KernelRTCPTest.SrsRtcpCompound_Decode* tests that failed on
develop, with asserts and ASAN heap-buffer-overflow, and pass now.

---------

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
